text:
tara: filing here - customer on Windows corp-managed machine can't finish quickstart. first TLS handshake fails in Node, then sdk retries and shows 503. they assumed billing blocked them because onboarding banner appeared.

 tara: command they ran (PowerShell):
```
$env:REDWOOD_API_KEY = 'pk_live_XXXXX'
node quickstart.js
```

 tara: error they pasted:
```
Error: unable to verify the first certificate (SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED)
... SDK retrying (attempt 2)
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
```

 niko: probably corporate TLS interception (Intune or enterprise firewall). On Windows Node uses its own cert store; adding corp CA to Windows cert store doesn't always help Node unless you restart and point to the right store or use `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`.

 support-bot: Workspace "green-lake" is trial and has basic quotas. Trial doesn't cause TLS verify errors; banner triggered by repeated request failures - UX issue.

 security: quick note: we should not advise `--insecure` or disabling verification publicly. Recommend adding CA to machine or using a secure devbox.

 tara: user can't get IT to add CA. They asked if support can provide a hosted devbox.

 niko: short-term workarounds we suggested:
- Run quickstart on a personal laptop or cloud devbox (fastest).
- Create a small cloud VM, install Node, and run sample.
- If IT will allow, export corp CA from company browser cert store and set `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=C:\path\to\corp-ca.pem` before running Node. Example (PowerShell):
```
certutil -enterprise -user -store Root > corp-ca.pem  # (example, depends on env)
$env:NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS = 'C:\Users\you\corp-ca.pem'
node quickstart.js
```

 niko: also for Docker on Windows Desktop you can mount the cert and set env var in container: `-v C:\Users\you\corp-ca.pem:/usr/local/share/ca-certificates/corp-ca.crt:ro -e NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/usr/local/share/ca-certificates/corp-ca.crt` then run `update-ca-certificates` in the container if the image supports it.

 tara: they ran `curl --verbose https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health` and got issuer=Corp-Intercept-Proxy and SSL: certificate verify failed. so confirmed interception.

 support-bot: Support action: offered temporary hosted devbox for onboarding. Customer accepted.

 niko: product/SDK notes:
- Docs: add "Windows corp-managed machines" troubleshooting with PowerShell certutil example and Docker mount + NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS examples.
- SDK: if TLS verify fails, print a clear diagnostic suggestion (do not mention insecure flag): "TLS verification failed. Common cause: corporate TLS interception. Try running quickstart from a non-managed machine or add your company's CA to NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS. See https://go.redwood.ai/quickstart-proxy for steps."

 tara: onboarding-bot message caused confusion. Action: change banner copy so it reads "Repeated request failures detected. This may be caused by local network proxies or trial quotas. If you see TLS verification errors, follow the proxy troubleshooting guide."

 security: created a short internal blurb reminding support not to instruct customers to disable cert checks.

 onboard-bot: Note added to workspace green-lake: "provide hosted devbox, update docs for Windows cert store guidance, clarify onboarding banner".

 niko: I'll open DOCS-921 (windows proxy steps) and SDK-422 (friendlier TLS message).

 tara: customer is using the hosted devbox now and completed onboarding. closing support case after docs + SDK change. thanks everyone :sparkles:
